Monica/Ben,

Forwarding a credit/extension request from Cadenza (June). They ask for $5k extra eval credits and a 7-day extension. Background: this account signed up in August; I approved a one-week extension in early September for PoC issues and we issued a small top-up in mid-September.

Ben — can you run a quick fraud/abuse check (multi-account, multiple top-ups, trial sequencing) and confirm there are no obvious patterns? Monica — what's the CS view on health of the pilot (Signal: usage, request cadence)?

If clean, I can authorize a manual top-up but prefer a short, conditional approval (monitoring + caps). If suspicious, we'll deny and ask for procurement paperwork and a signed MOP.

Thanks,
Alex

Looping in Billing and Ben. Quick summary from CS: pilot engagement is low (average daily tokens below threshold last 10 days), but we see a spike during demos. They have requested extensions twice already in the past 60 days (see attached previous-approval-chain.pdf). Procurement did sign an initial MSA but the billing contact has submitted three separate top-up requests under the same org id.

Ben — I've attached the usage snapshot and the historical approvals. Can you verify:
- whether the top-ups were requested from the same IP ranges or distinct accounts
- any correlation to low-quality/automated signups

If benign, I'd be comfortable approving a conditional $2,500 top-up + 7-day extension with a manual usage cap and daily monitoring. If anomalous, we escalate to Risk & Legal for recovery and block further auto-topups.

Thanks,
Monica

- previous-approval-chain.pdf (approval emails)
- usage-snapshot.csv (redacted)

All,

I ran the checks overnight.

Findings:
- Same org_id and billing email for all requests; however we see three distinct device fingerprints across requests and two different IP geolocations (US-West, US-East). No clear evidence of synthetic accounts.
- Usage pattern: bursts tied to demo windows, low sustained token consumption. No excessive parallel signups tied to this org in our telemetry.
- Historical top-ups: two prior manual top-ups totaling $4,200 in the last 60 days. No chargeback history.

Conclusion / recommendation:
- Approve a conditional $2,500 top-up and a one-week extension.
- Add a hard daily token cap of 50k tokens and enable near-real-time alerts to Risk for any unusual burst above 60k/day.
- Require procurement to sign a short credit waiver (DocuSign link) before activation. Finance to manual-invoice any future top-ups > $2.5k.

I've uploaded the usage CSV snapshot to drive and attached SOC2 summary that procurement requested in past threads.

If you approve this workflow I'll implement the top-up and flag the account for 30-day monitoring. If either of you want stricter action we can deny and route to Legal for recovery language.

Ben Carter
Fraud & Risk Analyst
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- usage-snapshot.csv
- SOC2_summary.pdf
